passage: Medical researchers investigating long-term astronaut health have discovered that extended exposure to microgravity affects more than just muscle strength and bone density. Recent studies show that fluid in the body shifts upward toward the head in low-gravity environments, placing pressure on the eyes and altering their shape. Some astronauts experience temporary vision changes during missions, while others develop longer-lasting issues upon returning to Earth. Scientists are exploring countermeasures, including specialized compression garments and adjustable spacecraft environments that simulate partial gravity. Although these solutions show promise, researchers caution that space agencies must continue studying the problem as missions to the Moon and Mars become more common. Understanding how microgravity impacts human physiology is essential for keeping astronauts healthy during increasingly ambitious space exploration.
